topic.title: Image Watermarking, Provenance, and Adversarial Evaluation
topic.overview: Image watermarks aim to support attribution or provenance by embedding detectable signals, while related methods protect styles or hide information. This cluster examines both construction and failure: removal, forgery, transfer, and evaluation of residual or semantic marks. Robustness includes preventing false attribution, not merely retaining a signal after ordinary image edits.
topic.whyItMatters: A detector’s positive result is useful only if the mark is difficult to forge and its interpretation is clear. Security evaluations must consider both missing genuine marks and falsely assigning an unrelated image to a source.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives study watermark attacks and neural steganography. Recent generative-model work adds latent and model-integrated marks alongside removal and copying studies. The 2026 evaluation examples distinguish artifact-based and semantic watermark properties, seeking more interpretable assessments across generators and watermark families.
openQuestions: How can provenance systems jointly resist erasure and false attribution?
Which benchmarks capture adaptive attacks without confusing visual quality with security?

papers.tldr: Noise Contrastive Diffusion improves text-to-image safety across random seeds by correcting harmful training gradients and learning pairwise safety preferences.

papers.title: Towards Trustworthy and Identifiable Virtual Face Generation
papers.tldr: TIVDiff generates identifiable virtual faces with preserved pose and expression and an imperceptible cue for legitimacy verification.

papers.title: Training-Free Coverless Multi-Image Steganography with Access Control
papers.tldr: MIDAS combines diffusion-based multi-image hiding with user-specific access control without requiring training.

papers.title: Watch Your Step: Information Injection in Diffusion Models via Shadow Timestep Embedding
papers.tldr: Shadow Timestep Embedding reveals diffusion timestep conditioning as a side channel for auxiliary information with attack and defense applications.

papers.title: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models
papers.tldr: Visual prompts can jailbreak image-editing models, while a training-free introspective reasoning defense improves safety in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: WMVLM: Evaluating Diffusion Model Image Watermarking via Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: WMVLM evaluates residual and semantic image watermarks with type-specific quality and security measures while generating interpretable explanations.
